# Results

<!-- generated by python/scripts/35_readme_results.py from committed results; do not edit -->

> **Synthetic data, scored against the generator's truth: not clinical performance.** Real model runs (CPU, 2026-10-26), not simulated; agreement with *simulated* reviewers is a dry run and isn't shown here. One leaderboard per capability; methods aren't ranked across them. Sources: `data/datasets/ladder/`, `data/datasets/answer_key/`, `data/deid/`. Summary: [README](../README.md#results).

### Phenotyping: periodontal status per chart

Every method that assigns one of the six periodontal statuses, on the same 240 synthetic review charts against the generator's truth: models that read only the chart note, the rule phenotypes that combine the whole record, and each evidence type alone. **Rank** is the 95% range of the method's rank by exact status, over the same chart resamples as its CI (paired bootstrap): "1–3" means it plausibly ranks anywhere from 1st to 3rd.

Numbers are per 100 charts. **Correct**: the right status (healthy, gingivitis, or periodontitis stage 1–4). **Periodontitis incorrectly assigned**: said periodontitis, the patient doesn't have it. **Periodontitis incorrectly ruled out**: the patient has it, the method said they don't. **Incorrect stage**: right that it is or isn't periodontitis, wrong stage (1 mild to 4 most severe), or healthy and gingivitis mixed up. **No answer (evidence not available)**: the method gave no status because what it reads wasn't in the record, e.g. no probing chart was taken. *Unsafe errors*: incorrect answers that could harm a patient if acted on, e.g. a missed stage 3–4. *Stage 4 correct*: of the stage 4 patients, how many it called stage 4. Easy / medium / hard: correct, out of 100, when the note states the 2017 diagnosis (L1), states it in older terms (L2), or leaves it to be inferred from the findings (L3). For statisticians: sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV for periodontitis yes/no, with no answer counted as no.

### De-identification

Every method on the 400 synthetic dental notes with fake PHI (2,714 identifiers, all tiers), ranked by sensitive text leaked (fewest first), with a Wilson 95% CI. Per-identifier results aren't saved, so there is no paired bootstrap: **Rank** is the range the intervals allow, from only the methods clearly above counting to every method whose interval reaches this one's counting.

Numbers are per 100. **Text that is sensitive (PHI) incorrectly leaked**: patient names, dates and IDs the method should have removed but left in (one character left counts). **Text that is not sensitive incorrectly scrubbed**: dental words that look like a name or code (Glickman, Gracey 11/12, 6-5-6) that the method removed. Leaking sensitive text risks patients; scrubbing text that isn't sensitive damages the note the AI reads, so read them together. *Unseen tier*: the notes no engine was written against. **ASQ-PHI**: 1,051 synthetic clinical queries (MIT); its text that is not sensitive is the queries with no PHI, out of 100 queries. **MACCROBAT**: 200 real, published case reports (CC BY 4.0); its sensitive text is the dates, its text that is not sensitive the clinical terms. [More on these numbers](deidentification.md#how-to-read-the-numbers).
